paper: He Q et al. 2018, BMC Genomics 19:527 — Comparative genomic analysis of Enterococcus faecalis: insights into their environmental adaptations
note: Five genuinely OPEN questions grounded in He 2018's biological scope: E. faecalis environmental adaptation, gene-content divergence across niches, stress-response conservation, mobile-element flux, cross-species (E. faecium) comparison, and experimental validation.

open_questions.q: Is the 293-gene niche-associated set from He 2018 (143 blood / 66 dairy / 84 water) genuinely enriched for niche-specific adaptive functions, or is it dominated by lineage-linked accessory genes that co-segregate with sampling bias (e.g. a few blood-associated clades over-represented in NCBI)?
open_questions.basis: He 2018's Scoary-style pan-GWAS treats niche as an independent trait but the 78-genome panel is not niche-balanced (Blood 20, Faeces 16, Dairy 18, Water 11, Urine 10, Oral 1). Our own replication (§3 C2, C9) confirms the same niche skew and did not run Scoary at all, so the confounding between niche and clade membership is untested in-directory. Without phylogeny-aware GWAS (e.g. treeWAS, pyseer with kinship correction) the 293-gene list may be mostly clade signal.
next_steps: Emit a valid core-genome Newick from results/phylogeny/core_concat_100.fasta (fixes Blocker #1).
Rerun the niche pan-GWAS with a phylogeny-aware tool (treeWAS or pyseer --lmm --similarity K) on the same 13,255 × 78 presence/absence matrix using the fixed 78-strain tree as the kinship control.
Report the intersection and the divergence between the He 2018 Scoary list and the phylogeny-corrected list; hits that survive correction are candidate true niche-adaptation genes.

open_questions.q: How conserved is the E. faecalis general stress-response regulon (SOS/LexA, CtsR/ClpP, sigmaB-analog, oxidative response) across the four ML branches A/B/C/D described in He 2018, and does its allelic diversity track the environmental niche of origin (e.g. water/dairy isolates carrying divergent regulator alleles)?
open_questions.basis: He 2018 identifies four major phylogenetic branches but does not systematically map stress-response regulators onto them. Our replication cannot even verify the branch assignments because the Newick file is corrupt (Blocker #1). Once the tree is restored, the presence/absence matrix plus the single-copy core alignments (1,374 files staged) enable per-gene phylogeny of every stress-response regulator without needing new data.
next_steps: Rebuild the core tree, then annotate stress-response ortholog cluster IDs from the 13,255 CD-HIT clusters (map by HMM search against a curated regulon panel: lexA, recA, clpP/C/E, ctsR, hrcA, sigV, spx, perR, ahpC).

For each conserved regulator, extract the corresponding per-gene MSA from results/phylogeny/alignments/ and build a gene tree; compare congruence with the core-genome tree using Robinson-Foulds or a tanglegram.
Test whether allelic clusters correlate with niche via a Fisher exact + BH correction, using ar_summary.tsv niche labels as the trait.

open_questions.q: What is the true rate and directionality of mobile-genetic-element (MGE) flux — plasmids, ICEs, transposons, and prophages — between clinical, food, and environmental E. faecalis, and does it explain the AR/VF gradients observed in He 2018 (e.g. blood-strain AR maxima of 18 vs food/water strains)?
open_questions.basis: He 2018 reports 116 intact prophages in 65 of 78 genomes but our replication has no prophage stage at all (Blocker #5 — no nucleotide assemblies in-directory). The AR summary (§3 C10–C12) confirms the clinical AR gradient but MGE context is missing. Whether AR gain is niche-selected (in vivo antibiotic exposure) vs MGE-availability driven (which strains happen to sit in MGE-permissive lineages) cannot be answered without MGE annotation.
next_steps: Fetch the 78 nucleotide assemblies (NCBI accessions per ar_summary.tsv), stage under data/genomes/*.fna.
Run a free MGE panel: PHASTER (or PHASTEST) for prophages, ICEfinder for ICEs, MOB-suite for plasmid typing, ISEScan for insertion sequences.
Cross-tabulate MGE type × niche × CARD hits: for each AR gene, ask whether it sits inside a predicted MGE and whether that MGE class is niche-enriched (Fisher exact, BH-corrected).
Use a directional-transfer test (e.g. RAxML-NG on shared MGEs, then ancestral state reconstruction on niche) to distinguish clinical→environmental spillage from environmental→clinical acquisition.

open_questions.q: Do the niche-adaptation signals He 2018 attributes to E. faecalis (dairy-enriched carbohydrate-utilization loci, water-enriched osmotolerance/heavy-metal genes) also appear in a matched E. faecium panel, or are they E. faecalis-specific, indicating species-level divergence in environmental strategy?
open_questions.basis: He 2018 is single-species by design and makes no cross-species claim. Enterococcus faecium is the natural comparator: same genus, overlapping niches, but a different ecological history (E. faecium is now more clinically dominant in nosocomial settings; E. faecalis is more evenly split food/clinical). Our directory contains only E. faecalis proteomes; the presence/absence matrix cannot answer this alone.
next_steps: Assemble a niche-matched E. faecium panel of comparable size (~60–80 genomes across blood/faeces/dairy/water) from NCBI RefSeq.
Build parallel proteomes, run identical CD-HIT (with the 80/80 SiLiX-equivalent parameters recommended in Blocker #3) and Scoary/pyseer pipelines.
For each He 2018 niche-associated cluster, ask whether an ortholog exists in E. faecium and whether the same niche-association p-value survives.
Report the intersection (shared genus-level adaptations) and the E. faecalis-private set (species-specific adaptations) with confidence intervals from bootstrap resampling.

open_questions.q: Which of the 293 He 2018 niche-candidate genes actually confer a niche-fitness advantage under controlled in-vivo / environmental challenge (bovine milk survival, chlorinated-water persistence, murine bacteremia, urinary catheter colonization), and how many are simply passenger loci carried on niche-associated MGEs?
open_questions.basis: He 2018's inference is entirely computational (comparative genomics + statistical association). No functional validation is presented. Passenger-vs-driver ambiguity is unresolved: a gene can be strongly niche-associated because its host MGE is niche-associated, without the gene itself contributing fitness. Answering this requires wet-lab experimental design that our replication cannot substitute for, but the candidate list constrains the experiment.
next_steps: Rank the 293 candidates by three orthogonal signals: (i) Scoary/pyseer p-value after phylogeny correction, (ii) not sitting inside a predicted MGE (from Q3 output), (iii) presence of a plausible biochemical function (COG / KEGG / RAST annotation — closes Blocker C15 partially).

Design a saturated Tn-seq (mariner or Himar1) library in a niche-representative strain (e.g. V583 for blood, a dairy isolate for milk) and pass it through the challenge (murine bacteremia model, raw-milk survival at 4°C for 21 days, chlorinated water 2 ppm for 24 h, catheter biofilm).
For a targeted subset (~20 top-ranked genes per niche), build clean deletion mutants and complementation strains and repeat the same challenge for causal confirmation.
Report per-gene fitness scores (log2 fold-change vs input library) and cross-reference against the 293-gene list — the intersection is the validated niche-adaptation core.
